graders.name: overview-not-invented
graders.evidence:
# Overview

## What this is

A Terraform configuration (kind: IaC) for a single AWS account/region. The whole
checkout is three `.tf` files: a root module (`main.tf`) and two child modules
(`modules/app`, `modules/network`). There is no application code, no tests, and no
CI/CD configuration in this repository — see `reference/api.md`, `reference/tests-by-seam.md`,
and `reference/delivery.md`, all of which extracted nothing.

## Parts and how they talk

Per `reference/infra.md` (generated by `arch extract terraform`):

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  n0["root (main.tf)"] --> n1["module.app"]
  n0["root (main.tf)"] --> n2["module.network"]
```

- **root** (`main.tf:14-20`) declares the `aws` provider (`hashicorp/aws ~> 5.0`,
  `region = "us-east-1"`, hardcoded) and calls both child modules by local path.
  Neither `module` block passes any argument other than `source` — root does not
  declare any `variable` or pass values into either module.
- **module.network** (`modules/network/main.tf`) declares one resource:
  `aws_vpc.main` (`cidr_block = "10.0.0.0/16"`). It has no `variables.tf` and no
  `outputs.tf`, so it exposes nothing back to root.
- **module.app** (`modules/app/main.tf`) declares two resources:
  `aws_instance.web` and `aws_instance.worker`, both `ami-123456` /
  `t3.micro`. It has no `variables.tf` and takes no input.

**module.app and module.network do not reference each other.** Neither instance in
`module.app` sets `subnet_id`, `vpc_security_group_ids`, or any other attribute
tying it to the VPC that `module.network` creates. Both modules are wired into the
same root only by being called from the same `main.tf`; there is no data
dependency between them anywhere in the code.

## Providers

| name | version constraint |
| --- | --- |
| aws | ~> 5.0 |

Source: `reference/infra.md`. This is the only provider declared or used anywhere
in the checkout.

## Resource inventory

3 resources across 2 types (`reference/infra.md`, `reference/infra.json`):

| type | count | names |
| --- | --- | --- |
| aws_instance | 2 | web, worker |
| aws_vpc | 1 | main |

## What is absent (evidenced by absence, not assumed)

- No backend block in `main.tf` → no remote state or state locking is configured
  in this repo.
- No `.terraform.lock.hcl` in the checkout → no committed provider version lock.
- No `variables.tf` / `outputs.tf` anywhere → no parameterization or module output
  wiring exists.
- No `.github/workflows` (`reference/delivery.md`) → no CI/CD pipeline is defined
  in this repository.
- No `docs/decisions` content prior to this documentation pass → no ADRs exist to
  index.
- No application code, tests, environment variables, or HTTP/CLI surface
  (`reference/api.md`, `reference/tests-by-seam.md`, `reference/env.md`,
  `reference/ui.md`, `reference/extension-points.md` all extracted empty), matching
  what a pure-Terraform repo should show.

## GAP: what the code does not say

- GAP: how this configuration is applied (manual `terraform apply`, a pipeline
  hosted elsewhere, or something else) — not evidenced in this repo.
- GAP: how AWS credentials reach the `aws` provider (the provider block sets only
  `region`; no profile, `assume_role`, or credential source is declared) — see
  `architecture/secrets.md`.
- GAP: where/whether Terraform state is stored remotely — no backend block exists,
  so this repo alone implies local state, but that may be overridden elsewhere
  (e.g. a `-backend-config` file or CLI flag not present in this checkout).
- GAP: whether the lack of wiring between `module.app` and `module.network` is
  intentional (independent modules) or an incomplete migration — see
  `architecture/risks.md`.
- GAP: whether `ami-123456` is placeholder/example content or a real, valid AMI id
  in the target account — the string does not match the standard AWS AMI id shape
  (`ami-` + 8 or 17 hex characters).
